The seventh tread still gave a little under her heel.

The door at the bottom was unbarred. She stood looking at it for a long moment before she understood that she had left it that way herself, hours ago, when she had gone up to trim the wick and had thought there was no one within forty miles to bar it against.

Outside the light had come full on. The rocks below were drying in patches, dark to pale, and the gulls had settled onto the shoal as if to lay claim to it before the water returned. She walked to the edge of the landing and looked down at the deep channel. Nothing floated there. Nothing had been dragged up. The water lay flat and ordinary and gave back the sky.

She unfolded the chart again in the wind and held it flat with both hands. The mark was small. A single line, a pencil's width, running from the open sea in past the shoal, past the tower, and ending at the little cove on the landward side where the old slip had rotted years ago. Not a wreck's line. A course. Deliberate, and finished, and ending here."}
